prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

The profile below describes the moral priorities of the British electorate.

TEXT_C:
This 2005 manifesto proposes changes across the economy, environment, welfare, public services, transport, democracy, and international policy.

Economy and taxation
- More progressive income tax bands (illustrative: 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and additional corporation tax bands (up to 40% on profits over £1.5m).
- Shift taxation from labour and consumption to resource use and pollution: abolish National Insurance, phase out VAT, introduce revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes (including aviation fuel; levies on plastic bags).
- Pilot a Land Value Tax set locally to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies, support for small businesses; oppose joining the euro; seek reform of global trade rules.
- Job creation via renewable energy, low‑carbon transport, and zero‑waste industries; defend workplace rights and reduce working hours.
- Supplement GDP with well‑being metrics (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: cut CO2 by 20% (2010), 50% (2020), 85% (2030); develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic energy VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; abolish standing charges; protect low‑use consumers.
- Reach 40% renewable energy by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; deploy solar, small‑scale wind, offshore wind/wave, and biogas.
- Warmer Homes Act to cut domestic energy demand 30% in 10 years; local “Smart Energy Councils” targeting 45% emissions cuts by 2020.
- Decommission nuclear plants at end of life; end nuclear R&D support.

Welfare, housing, work and families
- Phase in a universal, non‑means‑tested Citizen’s Income; retain specialist benefits and initially retain housing benefit.
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension, earnings‑linked, replacing Pension Credit.
- Simplify child support and increase child benefit in the first phase; end the Working Time Directive opt‑out; explore a 35‑hour week; expand early‑years centres.
- Boost affordable housing: let councils reinvest sale receipts, support self‑build co‑ops, apply LVT, and upgrade insulation/efficiency.

Health and education
- Restore a universal NHS free at point of use; end PPPs and resist service liberalisation.
- Abolish prescription charges; reintroduce free eye tests and NHS dental care; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Increase health funding to about 9% of GNP; consider a hypothecated NHS tax; redirect future defence savings to health.
- Increase education funding (pre‑school and post‑16), scrap tuition fees, restore maintenance grants, abolish SATs, and promote individual learning plans.

Transport
- Target a 10% road‑traffic reduction by 2010; divert £30bn from road building to public transport; re‑regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Reflect full motoring costs via congestion charging/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish car tax discs; vary freight duty by size/axle/pollution; fund R&D in efficient vehicles.
- Restrain aviation growth: oppose new runways, ban night flights, seek EU aviation fuel tax; tax domestic flight emissions; raise Air Passenger Duty; shift short‑haul to rail.

Environment, food, and animal welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration, reduce packaging, set recycled content standards, create a Zero Waste Agency; aim for 60% domestic recycling by 2010.
- Environmental Protection Commission; eco‑taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen chemicals regulation.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, and nanotechnology; oppose patents on natural resources.
- Animal welfare: extend hunting bans, replace vivisection, end live exports, ban battery eggs (including enriched), tighten broiler rules, ban fur imports.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local food chains; ban GM food.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies backing local markets, biodiversity, and sustainable incomes for farming and fishing.

Crime and justice
- Prevention through urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, more caretakers; treat drug use as a health issue; reject ID cards and redirect funds to prevention.
- Strengthen community policing, accountability, and local stations; revive community wardens/keepers.
- Tighten gun laws: quantitative lethality threshold, broader prohibitions, treat deactivated guns as active for licensing, single rigorous licensing, ongoing expert review.
- Expand restorative justice; enhance responses to hate crimes, violence against women; support stronger disability rights.

Democracy and constitutional reform
- Oppose national ID cards.
- Devolve power to local and regional levels; introduce proportional representation for local and national elections.
- Enable local recall (40%) and referenda (20% trigger); empower local taxation via LVT.
- Fully elected upper chamber by PR; draft a written constitution; disestablish the state church; limit monarchy’s formal roles.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while advocating EU reform to enhance democracy and sustainability.

International policy
- Ethical foreign policy: prioritise diplomacy, UN peacekeeping, and conflict prevention; withdraw troops from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers.
- Reduce defence spending to EU average; decommission nuclear weapons; end arms export subsidies/credits; negotiate an Arms Trade Treaty; ban use of depleted uranium.
- Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax; enable North–South carbon finance flows.
- Reform UN Security Council (end permanent seats; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Overhaul global trade rules to permit localisation and sustainability, replacing or modifying WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade.
- Asylum/migration: uphold refugee rights, speed decisions, allow work/benefits, provide independent appeals; ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention; review domestic asylum law; support improved EU standards.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals and commitments

- Economy and tax: Maintain a 2% inflation target and fiscal rules; keep net debt prudent. No rise in basic or top income tax and no VAT on essentials; targeted support for families. Deliver £21bn efficiency savings. Raise the minimum wage to £5.05 (Oct 2005) and £5.35 (Oct 2006). Aim for an 80% employment rate via welfare-to-work and Incapacity Benefit reform (Pathways to Work). Support enterprise, manufacturing and procurement; keep competitive corporation tax and R&D credits. Ten‑year science strategy to lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014. Energy policy to balance climate and security with renewables, nuclear, clean coal and microgeneration.

- Transport: Invest over £180bn to 2015; improve rail reliability, consider new high‑speed lines and fund Crossrail; upgrade London Underground. Expand key motorways, manage congestion and consider national road pricing. Free off‑peak local bus travel for over‑60s and disabled people; stronger local powers over buses; promote cycling, walking and road safety. Press to include aviation in EU emissions trading; expand UK shipping under tonnage tax.

- Education and skills: Personalised learning; multiyear school funding with a guaranteed per‑pupil uplift. All secondary schools to be specialist and extended; target at least 200 Academies by 2010; nationwide rebuilding of secondary schools (BSF) and a 15‑year primary upgrade. Stronger discipline and support for special educational needs. 14–19 reforms with specialised diplomas; more apprenticeships and reformed FE. In HE, fees capped at £3,000 with grants and bursaries; expand participation toward 50% and increase PhD support.

- NHS and public health: Investment tripling by 2008; maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment by 2008; free choice of hospital. Expand primary and community services, including modern community hospitals; use independent/voluntary capacity at NHS standards. Tougher action on MRSA and streamlined management. More NHS dentists; better patient information. Improve school meals and nutrition standards; clearer food labelling; curb junk food advertising to children. Restrict smoking in most enclosed workplaces and public places; expand cessation services and health trainers; universal access to school nurses.

- Crime, justice and security: Neighbourhood policing teams nationwide; expand Community Support Officers and a single non‑emergency number. Wider powers against antisocial behaviour and alcohol‑related disorder. Drug testing on arrest with compulsory assessment; establish the Serious Organised Crime Agency; restructure for regional/national threats. Violent Crime Reduction Bill (replica guns, knives, air guns); tougher sentences and comprehensive offender management with post‑release supervision and tagging. Stronger asset recovery; corporate manslaughter law. Borders: introduce a points‑based migration system, English for settlement, employer penalties, biometric visas, e‑borders and phased ID cards; faster asylum decisions. Counter‑terror measures including control orders and new offences.

- Families and older people: Halve child poverty by 2010–11 through tax credits, childcare and employment; expand Sure Start Children’s Centres to 3,500 by 2010; free nursery education to 15 hours/week (towards 20); extended schools 8am–6pm; broader childcare support. Increase paid maternity leave to 9 months in 2007 (aim for 12) and extend flexible working (consultations for carers/older children). For older people: Pension Credit maintained; free off‑peak bus travel; consult on long‑term pensions reform; end unjustified compulsory retirement before 65; right to request work after 65; individual care budgets and better support for carers.

- Housing and communities: Expand home ownership; raise the stamp duty threshold; focus new supply in growth areas and regeneration where demand is weak; widen shared ownership. Ensure all social housing is decent by 2010; increase new social homes by 50% by 2008; enable councils to build; expand choice‑based lettings. Rural support for post offices, buses, affordable homes; CAP/CFP reform; environmental stewardship; Animal Welfare Bill.

- Fairness at work and equality: Deliver a package including at least four weeks’ paid holiday in addition to bank holidays; enforce protections against discrimination (age, religion/belief, sexual orientation, gender, disability); narrow the gender pay gap; strengthen disability rights with personalised support. Create a Commission on Equality and Human Rights and a Single Equality Act.

- International, defence, development and climate: Active role in the EU (referendum on the Constitutional Treaty), with NATO as defence cornerstone; euro decision based on five economic tests. Counter WMD proliferation; support stability in Iraq and Afghanistan; pursue Middle East peace. Retain the independent nuclear deterrent; modernise armed forces; prioritise veterans. Development: reach 0.7% of national income for aid by 2013; debt relief; anti‑corruption; International Finance Facility; aim for universal AIDS treatment by 2010 and free basic health and education in poor countries. Climate: meet Kyoto; target −20% CO2 by 2010 and −60% by 2050; expand renewables, efficiency and emissions trading.

- Culture, sport, media, digital and environment: Free entry to national museums; renew regional museums; expand cultural access in schools; invest in grassroots sport and facilities; guarantee 2 hours PE plus 2–3 extra hours weekly by 2010; support the 2012 Olympics legacy. Reform BBC governance via a new Trust; guarantee the licence fee for the Charter; complete digital switchover 2008–2012; modernise IP and introduce film tax relief. Strengthen local environmental powers; universal kerbside recycling of at least two materials by 2010; focus new homes on brownfield; protect/enhance green belt; Marine Act; apply a sustainable building code for publicly funded homes from 2006.

- Democracy, devolution and local government: Complete House of Lords reform (remove remaining hereditaries, codify conventions, limit bill time; free vote on composition). Devolve further powers to Wales, London and regions; work to restore Northern Ireland institutions contingent on ending paramilitarism. Empower neighbourhoods with budgets, by‑laws and service triggers; extend parish councils to London. Support social enterprises in public services. Create a national youth volunteering framework. Give councils more freedoms, three‑year funding and fewer inspections; consider more elected mayors and whole‑council elections. Cap excessive council tax rises and improve take‑up of council tax benefit.
